speakers: Scott Bessent (Key Square Group founder, ex-Soros; named Treasury Secretary nominee)
summary: Real Vision interview (Nov 2024) with Soros/Druckenmiller-lineage macro investor Scott Bessent. Approach: theory, empirical proof, framing, Wall Street positioning as final check; hunt asymmetric trades where consensus says it cannot happen. Views: China decoupling and deflation export, gold accumulation, 7% US deficit with shortened maturities, Japan reflation (short yen trade lost on yen weakness), and a bifurcated US economy.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: we have a saying the micro drives the macro
claims.claim: The Soros-Druckenmiller style begins from equity research and company conversations about the real economy, then builds a macro mental model, rather than forecasting data prints.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: a lot of My Success in foreign exchange has been thinking like a corporate
claims.claim: FX views come from asking what would make a cash-rich corporation move money across borders or not repatriate earnings, i.e. corporate capital flows drive currency trends.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: we observe what's going on and we're looking for anomalies or systems that are either accelerating or could break down
claims.claim: Process: look for systems that are accelerating or about to break down, form a theory, prove it empirically, then check framing.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: we don't begin our process with something from the city from Wall Street uh but we do use it as the final check
claims.claim: Wall Street positioning and option skew are used as a final check; if the idea is already priced in (high positioning, skew), shelve it and do not trade.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: in the market today you can't really get a data Edge uh you probably don't want an information Edge
claims.claim: The achievable edge today is inferential or framing, not data or information; patience and saying no (Dr No) are part of the process.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: we could push the bank of England up against the bottom of the band and they had to buy an unlimited amount of Sterling
claims.claim: The 1992 ERM trade: the Bank of England was obliged to defend the 2.5% lower band by buying unlimited sterling, so the speculator could push until the peg broke.
claims.conditions: fixed exchange rate with obligation to defend

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: UK mortgages unlike long-term us mortgages floated the with the overnight rate
claims.claim: Floating-rate UK mortgages meant rate hikes to defend the pound crushed the housing market and thus the economy, so the defence was self-defeating.
claims.conditions: economy highly geared to short rates

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: these FL structures always take longer to break down than you think
claims.claim: Flawed policy structures take longer than expected to break, and the authorities lose less by abandoning a failed policy early.

claims.speaker: Ash Bennington
claims.quote: you were trying to create this unified currency uh in where capital is very mobile but economies are structured very differently
claims.claim: Fixed exchange arrangements between mobile capital and structurally different economies are flawed and eventually break.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: it's really the asymmetric nature
claims.claim: Great trades have asymmetric payoffs: small negative carry with large upside (Paulson subprime CDS: lose up to 25%, make 250-350%).

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: red red meat for us when someone said oh this this could never happen this has never happened this will never happen
claims.claim: Claims that something has never happened (US national house prices falling, China meltdown, reserve currency safe) mark asymmetric opportunities, because the structure that made it never happen has changed (national banking, CDOs, subprime).

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: the world was shocked that brexit happened
claims.claim: After Brexit and Trump 2016 the market panicked and crashed (S&P limit down on election night), but the shock reversed within weeks; buying the overreaction paid.
claims.conditions: political surprises with markets mispricing outcome
claims.testable: yes - event study of political shocks

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: if you're a fund manager you got brexit wrong you got Trump wrong you're not taking any chances that Marine lepen is going to be the president
claims.claim: Behavioural: after two prior surprises, managers over-hedged French election risk, so skew and euro puts became extreme.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: the market was paying me to take the risk then even on the night when he won the the Euro only went from 105 to 107
claims.claim: When option skew prices a political tail far above the plausible probability, take the other side; the euro rose only to 107-108 after Macron won.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: the US government is dependent on external financing
claims.claim: US-China decoupling is a bigger worry than a Taiwan war because the US government depends on external financing.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: a giant manufacturer that's exporting deflation what's the business model for Germany
claims.claim: China moving up the value chain exports deflation and threatens the business models of Korea and Germany.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: we're looking at all all the Chinese trade balances their trade with the developed World versus what's now called the global South
claims.claim: Gauges for China: trade balances with developed versus global South, repackaged exports, US tech sanctions, PBoC and yield curve, internal stress, external indicators, fund flows.
claims.indicator: Chinese trade balance split, bond yields, fund flows

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: in terms of foreign direct investment what would make a long-term investor put money in China right now
claims.claim: FDI is the better gauge of long-term confidence than portfolio inflows; no G20 corporation would build a factory in China now, though equities can bounce on portfolio flows.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: is there a 5 10 20% chance that if if you have R&B that your assets will be frozen
claims.claim: The yuan may be cheap on a normal equilibrium, but the other equilibrium is not getting money back (asset freezes, a Russia-type day for Chinese equities), a material tail risk.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: some of these funds are trading at 40 50 60 maybe even one at a 70% discount to stated nav people just want out
claims.claim: China venture capital and private equity funds trade at 40-70% discounts to stated NAV in the secondary market, showing institutions wanting out.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: real rates started going up in the US nominal rates started going up which is normally e even in an uptrend for gold is a signal that you're going to get a 5 10 could be 15% pullback
claims.claim: Gold rising 15% while real and nominal rates rose, when a pullback was normal, signals structural accumulation (central banks, global South, US consumers).
claims.direction: gold up despite higher real yields
claims.testable: yes - gold vs real yield regression residual

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: pboc buying and you've got Mom Moms and Pops going into Costco and buying
claims.claim: Central bank (PBoC) buying, global South and retail (Costco selling $100-200 million of gold bars monthly) show broad gold accumulation.
claims.indicator: central bank gold purchases, retail sales

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: my guess is that it's going to eventually be the dollar it could initially be rates
claims.claim: The release valve for unsustainable US fiscal and monetary policy will eventually be the dollar, possibly first rates; gold versus the dollar tracks this.
claims.indicator: gold priced in USD, long-term yields

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: the price appreciation of gold in the S&P since 1967 are are the same
claims.claim: Gold and the S&P 500 have had similar price appreciation since 1967 (gold ahead since 2000 excluding dividends).

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: kol would say we are going from A to B in gold and I don't really care what happens in between
claims.claim: Gold thesis is a long-term tectonic move from A to B with oscillations; the investor's skill is sizing up at the right times.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: we are running a 7% budget deficit with the no financial crisis no recession and no war this has never happened before
claims.claim: A 7% US deficit in peacetime expansion is unprecedented; the Treasury shortened issuance to bills, making debt service rise mechanically (about $1.1 trillion in 2024, higher than defence).

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: exactly the wrong thing to do is to move the maturities to the short end
claims.claim: Shortening US debt maturities makes the US behave like an emerging market and exposes the budget to the policy rate; interest costs could reach $1.6 trillion if rates are not cut.
claims.indicator: share of bills in debt, interest outlays

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: Goose The Market loosened Financial conditions
claims.claim: Treasury bill-heavy refunding and Powell's dovish press conferences in Nov-Dec 2023 loosened financial conditions, lifting stocks 25% and tightening high yield spreads, reigniting the economy.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: the FED failed the American people with the great inflation of 21 and 22
claims.claim: The Fed was late to hike and was doing QE until the month before the first hike in 2022, allowing inflation to run.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: we always try to like Focus what is the trade where where is the fulcrum and and we we try to keep it very simple
claims.claim: Implementation: find the one fulcrum trade and keep the portfolio simple.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: I don't really need to mess around in the jgb market because I don't know what the jgb market could do
claims.claim: The Abenomics trade was simple: short the yen and long Japanese equities, with no JGB exposure because JGB behaviour was uncertain.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: I like boring I'm boring I look for my portfolio to be boring I like to do easy things
claims.claim: A portfolio should be expressible simply (Soros: does it mean up or down); complexity (swaptions) is discouraged.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: we have been wrong this year is I thought it would result in Yen strength rather than Yen weakness
claims.claim: Despite correct Japanese reflation analysis, Key Square expected a stronger yen from policy normalisation and lost because the yen weakened further, a lesson that valuation does not drive currencies near term.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: it's 40% undervalued but as you know in currencies valuation never matters
claims.claim: The yen was 40% undervalued but valuation does not matter for timing currency moves.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: his popularity just continues to sink as the Yen continues to sink
claims.claim: Prime Minister Kishida's popularity was tied to the yen; a rational political response would be to act, but weakness persisted, and he expected him to be out in about two months.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: Japan's replating there was a 10year lag in or eight nyear lag in corporate governance
claims.claim: Japanese equities benefit from replating and a corporate governance catch-up; the Nikkei exceeded its 1989 high.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: interest rate hikes are actually stimulative to Japan so huge amount of personal savings large corporate savings
claims.claim: With large personal and corporate savings, rate hikes stimulate Japan's economy, so the BoJ need not fall prey to fiscal dominance (government unable to raise rates because of debt).
claims.indicator: BoJ rate hikes, household and corporate savings

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: fiscal dominance is just the government is unable to raise rates because the size of the debt is so large
claims.claim: Fiscal dominance is when the government cannot raise rates because of the debt size; the US is flirting with it and relies on foreign funding.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: you look like a US Bank in 1907 Without A lender of Last Resort
claims.claim: FTX lacked custody separation and risk management and was exposed to a run like a 1907 bank without a lender of last resort; a counterparty that dismisses basic questions should be avoided.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: I think it was the high status of his parents
claims.claim: Investors skipped diligence on FTX partly because of the founder's high-status parents; the more credentialed someone is, the more they should be examined.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: when people agree on a means of exchange it has value
claims.claim: Crypto has value when people agree it is a means of exchange; the next inflation hedge is unpredictable (Russian bicycles in 1998), so hold gold as the hedge.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: it's making the top 20% better off and you know we we know that I think the top 20% accounts for 40% of consumption
claims.claim: Easing financial conditions lifted asset prices, benefiting the top 20% who account for about 40% of consumption, while the bottom half carry debt: a bifurcated economy.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: credit card delinquencies are the highest that they've been since they've been started measuring them in 2012
claims.claim: Credit card delinquencies were at series highs (Philadelphia Fed, since 2012) in 2024, evidence of stress among those with debt rather than assets.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: this government spending is keeping rates high
claims.claim: Government spending (green New Deal) is keeping rates high and crowding young people out of housing.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: nobody on Wall Street is going to like what they have to say
claims.claim: The next election cycle could feature populists on both sides, with policy such as banning stock buybacks, a risk for equity valuation.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: where can you get yourself in front of the big Trend
claims.claim: Career advice: take risk, avoid fixed obligations, and find mega trends (e.g. leisure and gaming as AI frees time).

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: if you're in a big Trend the the big Trend covers up a lot of the mistakes
claims.claim: Being in a big trend covers up many mistakes in execution.
